text: OpenAPI provides a language-independent description of HTTP APIs so people and tools can understand operations, inputs and outputs without inspecting implementation code.
An OpenAPI paths section organizes available endpoints and HTTP operations. Each operation can document parameters, request bodies, responses and security requirements.
API response documentation should distinguish outcomes with appropriate HTTP status codes and schemas so clients can reliably interpret success and failure.
OpenAPI security schemes describe authentication mechanisms and security requirements can be applied globally or to individual operations.
A versioned API contract reduces ambiguity between producers and consumers and enables validation, documentation generation and automated testing.
Broken object-level authorization occurs when an API accepts an object identifier without verifying that the caller may access that object. Authorization checks are needed for every object access.

text: Broken authentication can let attackers impersonate legitimate users. APIs should protect credential flows, token validation and sensitive authentication operations.

text: Dockerfile instruction order affects build caching. Stable dependency steps should generally precede frequently changing application source to improve rebuild efficiency.

text: Starting a container does not guarantee its application is ready. Health checks and retry-capable clients help manage service startup dependencies.

text: C developers must validate allocation results, respect object bounds and pair every owned allocation with a well-defined release path.
Pointer operations require valid object lifetime, correct type and in-bounds arithmetic; dereferencing null, dangling or out-of-range pointers causes undefined behaviour.
Externally supplied sizes, indices and numeric values should be validated before they influence allocation, array access or arithmetic.
Signed overflow and unsafe conversions can invalidate security checks; programmers should reason about ranges before arithmetic or narrowing conversions.
Functions with several failure paths need a consistent cleanup strategy so files, memory and other acquired resources are released exactly once.
Resource Acquisition Is Initialization ties resource lifetime to object lifetime so deterministic destruction releases resources on normal and exceptional exits.
Modern C++ should express ownership explicitly and prefer scoped objects and standard smart pointers over raw owning pointers.
Interfaces should make preconditions, ownership and lifetime expectations clear while keeping implementation details hidden.
Using strong types, bounds-aware abstractions and standard containers reduces errors caused by casts, raw arrays and unchecked pointer arithmetic.
Shared mutable state requires a synchronization strategy; scoped locking and clear ownership reduce data races and forgotten unlocks.
Python provides high-level lists, tuples, sets and dictionaries; choosing the structure should reflect ordering, uniqueness, mutability and lookup needs.
Python exception handlers should catch the most specific useful exception, preserve diagnostic context and avoid silently hiding unexpected failures.
A with statement delegates resource entry and cleanup to a context manager, helping files and other resources close reliably when exceptions occur.
Developers must distinguish mutable from immutable objects and avoid unintended shared mutable defaults or aliasing across program components.
Modules group reusable definitions and packages organize modules into namespaces, supporting clearer separation and testability.
Go commonly returns an error value alongside a result; callers should inspect non-nil errors and keep the successful control flow clear.
A deferred call runs before the surrounding function returns and is useful for cleanup such as closing a file or unlocking a mutex.
A Go type satisfies an interface implicitly by implementing its methods, enabling behaviour-focused dependencies without explicit declarations.
Goroutines are lightweight concurrent functions and channels can coordinate communication, but lifecycle and cancellation still require deliberate design.
Go provides profiling, tracing and runtime diagnostics to investigate logic, concurrency and performance problems rather than relying on guesswork.
An OTT playback API should return an authorized playback resource plus clearly defined entitlement, expiry and error outcomes without exposing internal implementation details.
Playback endpoints must verify that the authenticated viewer may access the requested asset, territory and subscription tier; possessing a content identifier alone is not authorization.

text: HLS uses playlists to describe media variants and segments. A multivariant playlist lets a player select among renditions based on bandwidth and playback conditions.
source_title: HLS Authoring Specification for Apple Devices

text: A DASH MPD describes periods, adaptation sets, representations and media segment addressing so a compatible player can select and retrieve suitable media.
licence_note: DASH-IF publication terms; verify reuse requirements

text: Playback services should use stable contracts, bounded timeouts, traceable request identifiers and meaningful retryable versus non-retryable errors.
Using the HTML element that matches the content purpose provides built-in semantics and accessibility support to browsers and assistive technologies.
Form controls need programmatically associated labels so users can understand each input and activate controls reliably.
Meaningful images need useful text alternatives, while decorative images should avoid adding distracting information to assistive technology.
Interactive functionality must be operable with a keyboard, with visible focus and a logical navigation sequence.
Document source order should preserve meaning because screen readers and keyboard navigation commonly follow DOM order rather than visual positioning.
ARIA can supplement accessibility semantics for custom widgets but should not replace a suitable native HTML element when one exists.
Live regions can communicate important dynamic changes to assistive technologies, but excessive announcements can make an interface difficult to use.
WCAG 2.2 Level AA generally requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 for normal text and 3 to 1 for large text, subject to stated exceptions.
Focusable components should receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability when navigation sequence affects use.
Content should reflow within a constrained viewport so users can read and operate it without unnecessary two-dimensional scrolling.
CSS should not remove meaningful focus indicators or encode essential information through colour alone.
Custom JavaScript controls must expose correct names, roles, states and keyboard behaviour when native elements cannot be used.
Data tables need appropriate header cells and relationships so assistive technology can associate values with their row and column headings.
Clear link text, understandable instructions and plain language improve usability for people with varied cognitive and language needs.
Automated checks can identify some accessibility failures, but keyboard, screen-reader and human review are needed for many contextual requirements.
OTT player controls such as play, pause, seek, volume and captions need accessible names, keyboard operation and visible focus.
A player should expose available caption and subtitle tracks clearly and preserve understandable language and accessibility labels.
source_title: HLS Authoring Specification for Apple Devices
licence_note: Apple developer documentation terms; verify reuse requirements

text: Playback failures should be communicated in visible text and, when appropriate, announced accessibly without trapping focus or repeatedly interrupting the user.
The video player and its essential controls should remain operable at constrained viewport sizes without hiding controls or requiring unnecessary two-dimensional scrolling.
A Kubernetes Deployment declaratively manages a set of Pods, normally for stateless workloads, and controls updates through ReplicaSets.
The Deployment controller continually works to reconcile the observed workload state with the desired state declared in the resource specification.
A Kubernetes Service exposes a network application running on one or more Pods through a stable abstraction even when individual Pods change.
ConfigMaps store non-confidential key-value configuration and help separate environment-specific configuration from container images.
Kubernetes Secrets are intended for confidential values, but base64 representation is not encryption and etcd storage is unencrypted by default unless encryption at rest is configured.
Secret safety requires least-privilege access control, encryption at rest where appropriate and avoiding unnecessary exposure through environment variables or logs.
Persistent Volumes represent cluster storage independently of an individual Pod lifecycle, while claims express a workload request for storage.
A Dockerfile defines how a container image is built; a Compose file defines how one or more containers are configured and run together.
licence_note: Docker documentation terms; source repository Apache-2.0

text: Compose can create, start, stop and rebuild services while managing application networks and named volumes from one configuration.
licence_note: Docker documentation terms; source repository Apache-2.0

text: Operational diagnosis of a Compose stack includes inspecting service state, streaming logs and executing commands inside a running service when needed.

text: Prometheus stores data as time series identified by a metric name and a set of labels, with timestamped sample values.
Each unique label set creates a separate time series, so unbounded labels such as user identifiers can cause harmful cardinality growth.
Prometheus alerting rules evaluate expressions over time series and create active alerts when an expression returns matching vector elements.
An alert should describe a condition requiring action; duration controls can reduce noise from short-lived conditions before an alert fires.
Safe rollout practice includes observing rollout status, using readiness signals and retaining a rollback path when a new version is unhealthy.
OTT monitoring should distinguish service health from viewer experience using bounded labels and measures such as startup time, rebuffering, playback failures and manifest latency.

OTT alerts should represent actionable impact, for example a sustained rise in playback failures or manifest latency, and include service, region and runbook context without unbounded viewer identifiers.
Media-service rollouts need readiness checks, capacity observation, progressive exposure and a rollback path because a healthy process can still produce playback-impacting responses.
Environment-specific CDN endpoints, feature flags and non-secret playback settings belong in controlled configuration, while credentials and signing keys require secret handling.
Triage should correlate player symptoms with API, manifest, CDN and origin signals before assigning cause, using timestamps and request or session correlation identifiers.
A test assertion compares actual behaviour with an expected condition; the matcher should express the requirement being verified.
Playwright web-first assertions automatically wait and retry for expected UI state, reducing brittle manual timing logic.
Playwright locators identify elements and provide auto-waiting and retry behaviour for interactions and assertions.
User-facing locators based on role, label or visible text are generally more resilient than selectors tied closely to DOM implementation details.
Tests should be independent and control their own state so failure or execution order does not affect other tests.
Playwright can call REST APIs directly to test server behaviour, prepare test state and validate server-side postconditions.
API tests should verify status, response body and relevant postconditions rather than considering request completion alone sufficient.
pytest fixtures provide reusable setup data or services to tests through explicit dependency injection.
Fixture scope controls how often setup is created and reused; broader scope can improve speed but increases the need to avoid shared-state leakage.
Yield fixtures can place cleanup after the yield point so resources are released even when test logic fails.
Parametrization runs the same test logic against multiple input and expected-output combinations, supporting boundary and equivalence coverage.
Negative API tests should exercise invalid identifiers, unauthorized access, malformed inputs and limit boundaries.

text: A Playwright trace can preserve actions, DOM snapshots and network activity to support diagnosis of a failing test.
Replacing arbitrary waits with observable conditions and resilient locators reduces timing-related flakiness.
More test cases do not automatically mean better coverage; cases should be selected from requirements, risks, boundaries and meaningful state transitions.
Playback API tests should cover entitled and non-entitled users, expired tokens, territory restrictions, unavailable assets and expected status and error bodies.
HLS validation should check playlist syntax, referenced renditions and segments, media reachability and consistency of declared bandwidth, codecs and track metadata.
source_title: HLS Authoring Specification for Apple Devices
licence_note: Apple developer documentation terms; verify reuse requirements

text: Adaptive-streaming tests should exercise multiple renditions and constrained network conditions, confirming playback can switch representations without an avoidable fatal interruption.
licence_note: AWS documentation terms; verify reuse requirements

text: OTT tests should verify that expected audio, subtitle and caption tracks are present, correctly labelled, selectable and synchronized with the programme.
licence_note: AWS documentation terms; verify reuse requirements

text: Regression coverage should separate live and on-demand behaviour and include start-up, seeking where supported, discontinuities, end-of-content and recovery from transient segment failures.

text: An OTT device matrix should be risk-based, covering representative browsers, operating systems, screen sizes and playback capabilities instead of attempting every possible combination.
An Airflow DAG represents a workflow with a schedule, tasks and dependencies; tasks are the discrete units executed by workers.
DAG dependencies define execution order and data-flow relationships, while each task describes a specific unit of work.
Airflow tasks may execute on different machines and are isolated by default, so task communication should use supported mechanisms rather than local memory assumptions.
XComs let task instances exchange relatively small values and metadata within a DAG run.
XComs are not intended for large datasets; large data should be stored externally and referenced by a location or identifier.
A DAG schedule describes when workflow runs should be created; data interval and logical date semantics should be understood before designing incremental loads.
Data pipeline tasks should be designed so a safe retry does not unintentionally duplicate or corrupt output.
Reliable pipelines need observable failures, appropriate retries and clear ownership instead of silently continuing with incomplete data.
Python csv supports reading and writing delimited tabular data; explicit dialect, encoding and header handling reduce parsing ambiguity.
Python sqlite3 implements the DB-API interface for SQLite and supports parameterized statements for values.
Pipeline success should include data-quality checks such as expected schema, row counts, null constraints and accepted value ranges.
Capturing dataset inputs, outputs and task relationships improves impact analysis and investigation when data changes.
Backfills and historical reruns need partition-aware, idempotent logic and controls that prevent unintended overwrite or duplication.

Pipeline monitoring can represent duration, processed-record counts and failure totals as time series. Labels should stay carefully bounded because unbounded label values can cause harmful cardinality growth.
Alerts should identify actionable pipeline symptoms such as repeated failure, missing completion or breached latency thresholds.
OTT ingestion pipelines should validate identifiers, titles, hierarchy, availability windows, language, artwork references and required playback metadata before publication.
Series migrations need stable identifiers and explicit season and episode relationships so reruns do not duplicate content or detach episodes from their hierarchy.
Playback and content events can be published to Kafka topics and processed by consumers, but schemas, keys, ordering requirements and replay behaviour must be defined.
Analytics pipelines should detect duplicate, late and malformed playback events and document how sessions and QoE measures are derived before stakeholders use dashboards.
CSV or API migrations should reconcile source and target counts, rejected records, field mappings and representative samples while retaining an auditable error report.
